websearch.worst: D: a 2025 IEEE PVSC conference abstract on one device architecture is described as a 'three-year field-style study' and its result presented as a general finding
websearch.worst_summary_quote: A three-year field-style study: One 2025 study tracked devices over three years and found significant ion migration
websearch.worst_page_quote: Devices with a glass/FTO/compact-TiO2/mesoporous-TiO2/perovskite/Spiro-OMeTAD/Au architecture were fabricated and subjected to stability tests.
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader may think the 17% to 5% drop and lead-diffusion finding come from real-world field exposure and generalize across perovskite cells, when it is a short conference abstract on one lab architecture under stability tests.
websearch.notes: Other claims (extrinsic stressors, ion migration/trapped charges, residual strain, 500 h/1000 h/25 yr benchmarks, TiO2 UV hedge) match PMC5979782, PMC10811515, NWPU, PSAU pages. Joule/HZB item is from unfetched EurekAlert (fetch failed) and the summary honestly declined to report conclusions. Omits that extrinsic factors are often reversible vs trapped-charge irreversible. PMC and RSC pages blocked by reCAPTCHA in pagetext at first; PMC5979782 and Europe PMC full text worked.

webfetch.fetch_prompt: Summarize what this recent research paper on perovskite solar cells says limits their long-term stability. List the specific degradation mechanisms or factors (for example moisture, heat, light, ion migration, interface or contact degradation, phase instability) that the authors identify as the main constraints on long-term operational stability, and note any key quantitative findings that support them.
webfetch.worst: D: caveat on dark recovery dropped; summary implies reversible losses fully recover overnight, page says recovery only possible before permanent degradation occurs
webfetch.worst_summary_quote: Reversible losses can be fully recovered by overnight dark rest in one study
webfetch.worst_page_quote: Reversible losses could be only recovered before permanent degradation occurred
webfetch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader may believe overnight dark rest reliably restores efficiency, missing that recovery is lost once permanent degradation has set in.
webfetch.notes: Used Europe PMC full-text XML of PMC10811515 because pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov returned a reCAPTCHA page to pagetext. Result says it was truncated: page text 296570 chars, answer covers chars 0-100000 only (our raw extraction is ~108k chars, so extraction differs from WebFetch's rendering). Worst finding lies inside the read window (quote found in our raw text; the tool-side offset of that sentence cannot be confirmed, but the summary itself reports it). Minor omission: page says one-year ISOS-L lifetime was first reached in 2017 and has not improved since; summary omits the stagnation. Other checked numbers (0.58/0.84/2.31 eV, 80% RH, 40% loss after 40 h, 85 C/24 h, -15 to 65 C, 25% PCE) match.
